newsitem.title: USA: U.S. white wheat hit by demand drop, supply rise.
newsitem.headline: U.S. white wheat hit by demand drop, supply rise.

text.p: Bids for old crop U.S. white wheat sagged this week in reaction to a dearth of export demand, increased farmer selling and improved crop conditions, cash merchants and futures traders said Friday.

One milling source in the Pacific Northwest said Pakistan's decision last week to buy Australian white wheat instead of U.S. wheat was the equivalent of a pin prick in what had become an inflated old crop white wheat market.
"What's happening is that old crop white wheat had gotten itself into a great big inverse with the new crop, and that inverse is just falling apart," the milling source said.

Pakistan announced last Thursday that it planned to buy 378,000 tonnes of Australian white wheat for delivery in June and July, dashing U.S. exporters' hopes of making one more big export sale before the new crop comes on line.

"When Pakistan said they were buying from the Aussies, people started realizing that maybe the last of the old crop business was done," the source said. "The inverse was so high, and now people are just consolidating."
A trader at the Minneapolis Grain Exchange said that until recently, old crop white wheat had been trading at around 50 cents over new crop values.
Cash sources said the downturn in prices was compounded by active farmer selling Wednesday and Thursday.
"It was a thin market and it didn't take much selling to knock it down hard," a Portland cash source told Reuters Thursday.
Sources said white wheat prices also suffered on good crop condition ratings in Washington state, where harvest usually begins in early July and continues until early September.
In the most recent crop progress report issued June 2 by the Washington Agricultural Statistics Service, 86 percent of the wheat crop was rated in good to excellent condition.
That marked a dramatic increase from the previous week's rating of 68 percent good to excellent.
On Thursday, White wheat bids were down 22 cents a bushel in Portland and 18 cents in other parts of Oregon.
MGE July white wheat futures settled down only seven cents per bushel Thursday, but at one point during the session the July contract had been as much as 17 cents lower.
White wheat in Portland was being bid Friday at $4.30 per bushel, unchanged from Thursday. The July futures contract had not traded as of 1215 CDT Friday.
